To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) AS sourced rainfall was more variable compared to BoB sourced rainfall, 2) the AS sourced rainfall was responsible for the changes observed in vegetation composition and fluvial architecture in western India, and 3) AS sourced rainfall in western India was more variable and C3 plants were relatively more abundant during the last 75 ka.
The amount-effect based reconstruction of monsoon rainfall from the Gujarat alluvium revealed two distinct dry phases (75-60 and 30-10 ka) and a wet phase (60-30 ka).
